extracted.intended_audience: peer reviewers (referees) for Nature Portfolio journals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and policy for referees preparing reviews of manuscripts submitted to Nature Portfolio journals, covering criteria for publication, how to write reports, confidentiality, anonymity options, timing, AI policy, and related editorial procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for publication
rubrics_metrics.description: In general, to be acceptable, a paper should represent an advance in understanding likely to influence thinking in the field, with strong evidence for their conclusions. There should be a discernible reason why the work deserves the visibility of publication in a Nature Portfolio journal rather than the best of the specialist journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess both conceptual advance (novelty, influence on the field) and strength of evidence; consider whether the paper merits visibility in a Nature Portfolio title versus a specialist journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial triage (selection for formal review)
rubrics_metrics.description: All submitted manuscripts are read by the editorial staff. To save time for authors and peer-reviewers, only those papers that seem most likely to meet our editorial criteria are sent for formal review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect initial desk rejections for insufficient general interest, lack of novelty, or inappropriateness; editorial decisions may be based on informal advice from specialists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of the review
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary purpose of the review is to provide the editors with the information needed to reach a decision but the review should also instruct the authors on how they can strengthen their paper to the point where it may be acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write reports to inform editorial decision-making and to give actionable guidance to authors; negative reviews should explain major weaknesses so authors can improve the work for resubmission elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide reasoned arguments (not just recommendations)
rubrics_metrics.description: The most useful reports ... provide the editors with the information on which a decision should be based. Setting out the arguments for and against publication is often more helpful to the editors than a direct recommendation one way or the other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give clear, evidence-based reasoning for opinions; avoid unsubstantiated assertions; explain trade-offs rather than only stating 'accept' or 'reject'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Willingness to review revisions and provide follow-up advice
rubrics_metrics.description: When reviewers agree to assess a paper, we consider this a commitment to review subsequent revisions. We therefore ask that reviewers should be willing to provide follow-up advice as requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to re-evaluate revised manuscripts; editors may not re-send a paper if authors have not made a serious attempt to address criticisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting peer-reviewers — criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer selection is critical ... we base our choice on many factors, including expertise, reputation, specific recommendations and our own previous experience of a reviewer's characteristics. For instance, we select referees who are quick, careful and provide reasoning for their views, whether robustly critical or forgiving.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors look for technical expertise and reliable reviewing behavior (timeliness, thoroughness, justified opinions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Online manuscript review submission
rubrics_metrics.description: We ask peer-reviewers to submit their reports via our secure online system by following the link provided in the editor's email.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the journal's secure system and available online help; contact helpdesk for technical problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to the literature
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reviewer does not have access to any published paper that is necessary for evaluation of a submitted manuscript, the journal will supply the reviewer with a copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request necessary references from the handling editor (provide publication reference); the editor will obtain and send the paper, paying any necessary fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key results (what to summarise)
rubrics_metrics.description: Key results: Please summarise what you consider to be the outstanding features of the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin reports with a concise summary of the manuscript's main findings and their significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validity (fatal flaws and detailed critique)
rubrics_metrics.description: Validity: Does the manuscript have flaws which should prohibit its publication? If so, please provide details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and describe any methodological, analytical, or interpretational flaws that undermine validity; be specific about why issues are fatal or fixable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Originality and significance: If the conclusions are not original, please provide relevant references. On a more subjective note, do you feel that the results presented are of immediate interest to many people in your own discipline, and/or to people from several disciplines?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess novelty relative to the literature and the potential breadth of interest; supply references if relevant work has been overlooked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data & methodology (including supplementary material)
rubrics_metrics.description: Data & methodology: Please comment on the validity of the approach, quality of the data and quality of presentation. Please note that we expect our reviewers to review all data, including any extended data and supplementary information. Is the reporting of data and methodology sufficiently detailed and transparent to enable reproducing the results?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check methods detail, data integrity, completeness of supplementary files, and reproducibility. Recommend additional experiments or clarifications if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate use of statistics and treatment of uncertainties
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriate use of statistics and treatment of uncertainties: All error bars should be defined in the corresponding figure legends; please comment if that’s not the case. Please include in your report a specific comment on the appropriateness of any statistical tests, and the accuracy of the description of any error bars and probability values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate statistical methods, correctness of tests, clarity of error reporting, and whether uncertainty is properly characterized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclusions (robustness of interpretation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conclusions: Do you find that the conclusions and data interpretation are robust, valid and reliable?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether conclusions are supported by the data and analyses; flag over-interpretation or unsupported extrapolations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested improvements (what to request in revisions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggested improvements: Please list additional experiments or data that could help strengthening the work in a revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide specific, feasible suggestions for experiments, analyses, or clarifications that would address weaknesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: References (appropriateness and omissions)
rubrics_metrics.description: References: Does this manuscript reference previous literature appropriately? If not, what references should be included or excluded?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out missing key citations or unnecessary/irrelevant citations; provide suggested references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and context (abstract/introduction/conclusions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarity and context: Is the abstract clear, accessible? Are abstract, introduction and conclusions appropriate?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess readability, structure, framing of results for readers across disciplines where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inflammatory or potentially libelous material
rubrics_metrics.description: Inflammatory material: Does the manuscript contain any language that is inappropriate or potentially libelous?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag problematic language and recommend neutral, factual phrasing; editors may act to remove offensive content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity, equity and inclusion considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Springer Nature is committed to diversity, equity and inclusion; please raise any concerns that may in your view have an impact on this commitment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify issues that could impact DEI (e.g., sampling biases, exclusionary language) and state concerns in the report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declare scope limits of reviewer expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Please indicate any particular part of the manuscript, data, or analyses that you feel is outside the scope of your expertise, or that you were unable to assess fully.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State which sections you could not evaluate so editors can seek additional expertise if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address specific questions from the editor
rubrics_metrics.description: Please address any other specific question asked by the editor via email.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond directly to editorial queries in your report; these may concern specific technical points or ethical issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justify statements with facts and citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports ... should document the referees’ thought process. All statements should be justified and argued in detail, naming facts and citing supporting references, commenting on all aspects that are relevant to the manuscript and that the referees feel qualified commenting on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid unsupported opinions; where possible cite papers, data, or specific parts of the manuscript to back up critiques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential comments to the editor should not contradict author-facing comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidential comments to the editor are welcome, but they should not contradict the main points as stated in the comments for transmission to the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use confidential comments for sensitive matters but keep public and confidential advice consistent in substance.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI use policy for peer reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: We ask that, while Springer Nature explores providing our peer reviewers with access to safe AI tools, peer reviewers do not upload manuscripts into generative AI tools. If any part of the evaluation of the claims made in the manuscript was in any way supported by an AI tool, we ask peer reviewers to declare the use of such tools transparently in the peer review report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not put manuscript text into external generative-AI services; transparently declare any AI assistance used in composing the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and responsiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: We therefore ask reviewers to respond promptly within the number of days agreed. If reviewers anticipate a longer delay than previously expected, we ask them to let us know so that we can keep the authors informed and, where necessary, find alternatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept or decline promptly; notify editors early about delays; timely delivery supports rapid editorial decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymity and signing reports
rubrics_metrics.description: We do not release referees' identities to authors or to other reviewers unless a referee voluntarily signs their comments to the authors. To increase the transparency of the reviewing process, reviewers may sign their reports, if they feel comfortable doing so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider pros and cons before signing: reports are shared with other reviewers and across Nature Portfolio journals on transfer; avoid identifying yourself to authors while a manuscript is under consideration without telling the editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-anonymized peer review option
rubrics_metrics.description: Some Nature-branded journals and Communications journals offer a double-anonymized peer review option. Authors who choose the double-anonymized peer review option at submission remain anonymous to the referees throughout the consideration process. The authors are responsible for anonymizing their manuscript accordingly; a checklist is provided to help with this process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If participating in a double-anonymized review, assess the manuscript without author identity cues and follow anonymization checklist; journal-specific details on availability apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent peer review policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature and other selected Nature Portfolio titles follow a transparent peer review scheme, where we publish details about the peer review process as part of the publication (including the reviewer comments to the authors, author rebuttal letters, as well as the editorial decision letters in some cases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that reviewer reports and author rebuttals may be published alongside accepted papers (with opt-out rules depending on submission date); confidential comments and some editorial discussions are not published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing referees' reports
rubrics_metrics.description: As a matter of policy, we do not suppress reviewers' reports; any comments that were intended for the authors are transmitted, regardless of what we may think of the content. On rare occasions, we may edit a report to remove offensive language or comments that reveal confidential information about other matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid needless offence in tone; express opinions plainly but professionally. Editors may redact reports only for offensive/confidential content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer-review publication policies and confidentiality obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: All contributions selected for peer review are sent to at least one, but usually two or more, independent reviewers, selected by the editors. Authors are welcome to suggest suitable independent reviewers and may also request that the journal excludes one or two individuals or laboratories. Editors, authors and reviewers are required to keep confidential all details of the editorial and peer review process on submitted manuscripts. If a reviewer wishes to seek advice from colleagues while assessing a manuscript, the reviewer must consult with the editor and should ensure that confidentiality is maintained and that the names of any such colleagues are provided to the journal with the final report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not disclose or publish correspondence, reports, or confidential material without prior written consent; when consulting colleagues obtain editor approval and provide names.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature's rights on misconduct and disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature Portfolio reserves the right to contact funders, regulatory bodies, journals and the authors’ institutions in cases of suspected research or publishing misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you suspect misconduct, raise concerns confidentially with the editor; the journal may escalate to appropriate authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics, security and seeking additional advice
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature Portfolio journal editors may seek advice about submitted papers not only from technical reviewers but also on any aspect of a paper that raises concerns. These may include, for example, ethical issues or issues of data or materials access. Very occasionally, concerns may also relate to the implications to society of publishing a paper, including threats to security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag ethical, data-access, biosafety, dual-use, or societal-risk issues to the editor; the editor has ultimate responsibility for publication decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goals of peer review (identify flaws, suggest improvements, assess novelty)
rubrics_metrics.description: The goals of peer review are both lofty and mundane. Peer review is designed to select technically valid research of significant interest. Referees are expected to identify flaws, suggest improvements and assess novelty. If the manuscript is deemed important enough to be published in a high visibility journal, referees ensure that it is internally consistent, thereby ferreting out spurious conclusions or clumsy frauds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance stringency with openness to novel ideas; understand that reviewers cannot be expected to detect cleverly concealed, deliberate deceptions and that editors must balance competing claims across submissions.
